ko.broken: The move broke down, try again

sortir.name: Build out
sortir.book: Build out: the ball is with the keeper or the defenders and the opponent is pressing. It is done when the free man receives behind the first line. “Playing out short is a means, not a dogma.” (chapter 5)

progresser.name: Progress
progresser.book: Progress: a teammate can receive facing forward with space, free between the lines, or space opens in behind. Look forward first. (chapter 5)

fixer.name: Pin
fixer.short: Draw them in to free a teammate
fixer.book: Pin: the line ahead is closed or the block has shifted across. Draw them to one side to free a teammate on the other. (chapter 5)

finir.name: Finish
finir.short: Shoot, or find someone in the box
finir.book: Finish: the ball enters the final third with an advantage. Shoot from the finishing zone or find a teammate at the edge of the box. (chapter 5)

respirer.name: Breathe
respirer.book: Breathe: keep the ball with the safest pass and make the opponent run. “Breathing is not hanging on, it is making the opponent run” (chapter 5)

lecture.title: Reading the game
lecture.question: What is your pass setting up?
lecture.intro: A real situation stops at the moment our player receives the ball. You read the game the way the book teaches it: first the intention, then the receiver. The geometry of the passing lanes decides, then the action plays out.
lecture.step1: Choose the intention, one of the five in The Njangi Code.
lecture.step2: Tap the teammate who serves it, or the goal to shoot.
lecture.step3: Read the feedback, then watch how the action continues.
lecture.askIntention: What is your pass setting up?
lecture.askReceiver: {{intention}}: who gets it? Tap the teammate.
lecture.tapHint: Tap a numbered teammate (keys 1 to 9 on the keyboard).

notValid.sortir: Nobody is pressing here: there is no press to get out of.
notValid.progresser: No forward pass is open with space for the receiver.
notValid.fixer: The line ahead is not closed: no need to draw them in, you can go forward.
notValid.finir: No advantage to finish with: too far out, or the angle is closed.
notValid.respirer: Breathing here, under pressure and close to our goal, is playing with fire.

notes.shotFar: Shot from too far out: the finishing zone is closer to goal.
notes.shotBlocked: A defender is blocking the line of the shot.
notes.laneClosed: Lane closed: {{who}} is cutting the passing lane.
notes.laneTight: Tight lane: the pass only just gets through.
notes.pressedOnArrival: The receiver will be under pressure when the ball arrives.
notes.lineCrossed: The pass breaks through an opposing line.
notes.forcedLine: A pass forced into a closed line: the most dangerous loss of all.
notes.sidewaysGood: A sideways pass is right when it serves Pin or Breathe.

notServing.sortir: This choice does not find the free man behind the first line.
notServing.progresser: This choice does not move the ball forward.
notServing.fixer: This choice draws nobody in and does not switch the play.
notServing.finir: This choice leads to no shot and no ball into the box.
notServing.respirer: This choice takes a risk: breathing means the safest pass.

lecture.legend: On the pitch: your pass in gold, the best answer as a dotted line, the lanes in green (open), yellow (tight) and red (closed).
lecture.summaryHigh: You read the game through the eyes of The Njangi Code.
lecture.summaryMid: Your reading is coming along. Go back over the intentions you missed in chapter 5.
lecture.summaryLow: Take your time: look forward first, then ask yourself what the pass is setting up.

dix.title: Ten-pass challenge
dix.subtitle: From the keeper to the net: the Njangi goal
dix.objective: Start from the keeper, make the ball travel through at least ten completed passes, then score. Everyone puts in their share: if all eleven have touched the ball, the pot is full.
rules: The ball starts from the keeper.
At least ten completed passes before the goal. A goal with fewer passes does not count for the challenge.
Every time the ball is lost, the sequence starts again from the keeper (drill sheet G06, part 2).
Six opponents defend: two forwards, one midfielder, three defenders, and their keeper.
Bonus: all our players touched the ball during the sequence.
dix.adaptation: A game challenge inspired by Ball Lesson no. 40 “The Njangi goal” (Lionceaux, book 1) and by drill sheet G06 of The Njangi Code. The count of ten passes is a game rule: the book has all eleven players touch the ball, and the sheet asks for at least eight.

help.dribble: Tap the ball carrier, then the spot they carry the ball to.

analyse.title: Video analysis
analyse.intro: Every attempt in the Academy and the Challenge is recorded. Watch it again in slow motion, frame by frame, with the ball's path, the carrier's passing lanes and the opposing lines: the freeze frames of chapter 6 and the analyst's video of chapter 33, on your own actions.
analyse.emptyBody: Play a drill: your attempt will be ready to analyse here. The last six are kept on this device.
analyse.hint: Tap a player to follow their run. Keyboard: Space, arrows (Shift for 10 frames), C for the camera.

parcours.title: Development path
parcours.intro: Each drill sheet in the book trains specific competences and intentions. Your Academy stars draw your path here, and the game suggests the drill that will help you improve the most.
parcours.skillsHint: Share of the stars earned on the drills that train each competence. Levels 1 to 4, like the book's grid, measured here in the game.
parcours.intentionsHint: Drills completed among those that work on each intention.
parcours.note: These levels measure what you achieve in the game. They do not replace the coach's assessment on the pitch.
